newsitem.title: BELGIUM: RENAULT BELGIUM SALES DROP SHARPLY IN MARCH.
newsitem.headline: RENAULT BELGIUM SALES DROP SHARPLY IN MARCH.

text.p: Sales of French carmaker Renault in Belgium plunged nearly 43 percent in March, the month following the firm's shock declaration it would close its profitable plant at Vilvoorde near Brussels.
FEBIAC, the Belgian automobile manufacturers federation, said Renault sales in March fell to 2,861 units compared to 4,983 in the same month last year.
At the same time overall car sales in Belgium dropped 13.3 percent to 39,329 units from 45,352 in March 1995, FEBIAC said.
The announcement of the Vilvoorde closure, with the loss of 3,100 jobs has sparked protests in Belgium and France.

Vilvoorde workers have been occupying the factory since the announcement of the closure on February 27, and have joined in protest actions with their colleagues from Renault plants in France and Spain.
Several Belgian regional authorities and government ministries have cancelled orders for Renault vehicles in solidarity with the Vilvoorde workers.
Renault's share of the Belgian new car market dropped to 7.2 percent in March from 10.9 percent a year ago, FEBIAC said.
Renault workers plan a coordinated protest action in Brussels, Paris and Madrid on Friday.
